mainTopic: Following בית שמאי or בית הלל consistently; where the וושט is valid for שחיטה; a וושט torn from the jaw; and the start of the cut windpipe discussion.
overview: The ברייתא ends by saying a person must follow either בית שמאי or בית הלל consistently, and not collect only the stringencies of both. The גמרא settles a contradiction inside that ברייתא: either the two lines come from before and after the בת קול, or the permission line follows רבי יהושע, who ignores a בת קול. Still, רבא's ruling seemed to take two clashing חומרות. רב טבות answers that both come from רב, as רמי בר יחזקאל reports. The גמרא then defines the area of the וושט where שחיטה works, from a hand's grip at the top down to where it becomes hairy, and settles a challenge from רב's statement about the bottom טפח. Next, שמואל rules that a וושט torn off the jaw is כשר. After challenges about uprooted סימנים, this is narrowed to a וושט mostly peeled off in one piece. Finally the גמרא turns to a cut windpipe, which is טרפה when most of it is cut, and begins asking how that majority is measured.

steps.title: Don't collect only the stringencies of both schools
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says that a person who takes on the חומרות of both בית שמאי and בית הלל is called a fool. He must follow one school consistently, with both its leniencies and its stringencies.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who takes on the stringencies of בית שמאי and also the stringencies of בית הלל, the פסוק calls him 'the fool who walks in darkness.' Instead, if he follows בית שמאי, he should follow both their leniencies and their stringencies. If he follows בית הלל, he should follow both their leniencies and their stringencies.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the closing part of a ברייתא. It says you can't mix and match the two schools, even if you only pick the strict sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier part of the ברייתא already called someone who picks only the leniencies of both schools a רשע. Here it adds that picking only the stringencies of both is also wrong, and calls that person a כסיל (fool). The rule is consistency: choose one system and keep all of it.

keyTerms.meaning: Stringencies; the strict rulings
Leniencies; the lenient rulings
A fool
Rather; instead

steps.confusionAlert: Being strict on everything might sound like the 'safe' choice. The ברייתא says it is not: mixing both schools' stringencies is itself called foolish.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets out a basic principle of how to follow a מחלוקת. You commit to one consistent opinion and don't cherry-pick from both sides.

phrases.aramaic: מֵחוּמְרֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּמֵחוּמְרֵי בֵּית הִלֵּל –
phrases.english: (One who takes) from the stringencies of Beit Shammai and from the stringencies of Beit Hillel —
about him the verse says:
"The fool walks in darkness."
Rather, if like Beit Shammai —
like their leniencies and their stringencies;
if like Beit Hillel —
like their leniencies and their stringencies.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵחוּמְרֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּמֵחוּמְרֵי בֵּית הִלֵּל עָלָיו הַכָּתוּב אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from before this section, which discussed following the leniencies of both schools.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person may not adopt only the stringencies of both schools. He must follow one school fully, with its leniencies and its stringencies.

steps.title: The ברייתא seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא says the הלכה always follows בית הלל, but also says a person may follow בית שמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ברייתא itself is difficult. You said the הלכה always follows בית הלל, and then it teaches that someone who wants to act like בית שמאי may do so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא for contradicting itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the הלכה is 'always' like בית הלל, then following בית שמאי should not be allowed. Yet the same ברייתא permits it. Both lines cannot stand as they are.

keyTerms.meaning: This itself is difficult; the source contradicts itself
Always
And then it teaches
The binding law

phrases.english: This itself is difficult:

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרַתְּ: לְעוֹלָם הֲלָכָה כְּדִבְרֵי בֵּית הִלֵּל,
phrases.english: you said: the halakha is always in accordance with the words of Beit Hillel,
and then it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: וְהָרוֹצֶה לַעֲשׂוֹת כְּדִבְרֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי יַעֲשֶׂה!
phrases.english: "and one who wishes to act in accordance with the words of Beit Shammai may do so!"

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא גּוּפַאּ קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After quoting the ברייתא, the גמרא now challenges its internal consistency.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's two statements: 'the הלכה always follows בית הלל' and 'one may act like בית שמאי'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A fixed ruling for בית הלל seems to rule out any permission to follow בית שמאי.

steps.title: Before and after the heavenly voice
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the permission to choose was given before the בת קול. The ruling that the הלכה always follows בית הלל came after the בת קול.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here, it was before the בת קול. There, it was after the בת קול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by saying the two lines come from two different time periods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the בת קול announced that the הלכה follows בית הלל, a person could choose either school. After the בת קול, the הלכה was fixed like בית הלל. So the two statements don't clash, because each belongs to its own time.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult
Here... there; splitting two statements into two situations
A heavenly voice
Before / after

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here — before the Divine Voice;
phrases.notes: This 'here' is the line saying you may follow בית שמאי if you want.

phrases.english: there — after the Divine Voice.
phrases.notes: This one is the line saying the הלכה is always like בית הלל.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, כָּאן קוֹדֶם בַּת קוֹל, כָּאן לְאַחַר בַּת קוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting by time: the two statements refer to different periods.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both statements seemed to apply at the same time, so they contradicted each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Freedom of choice applied before the בת קול. The fixed ruling for בית הלל applies after it.

steps.title: Even after the voice, according to רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: even after the בת קול, one may follow בית שמאי. This part of the ברייתא follows רבי יהושע, who says we ignore a בת קול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you like, say: even after the בת קול. This follows רבי יהושע, who said we pay no attention to a בת קול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different answer. It says both lines can apply after the בת קול, because the permission line follows רבי יהושע's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע holds that a בת קול cannot decide הלכה. So for him, the בת קול's announcement doesn't settle the מחלוקת, and one may still follow בית שמאי. On this answer, the two lines of the ברייתא reflect different opinions rather than different times.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say; introduces an alternative answer
Even after
We pay no attention to a heavenly voice in deciding הלכה

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to the contradiction. (1) The permission was before the בת קול and the fixed ruling after it. (2) Even after the בת קול, the permission follows רבי יהושע, who ignores a בת קול in הלכה.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
even after the Divine Voice,
and it is (the view of) Rabbi Yehoshua,
who said: we pay no attention to a Divine Voice.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא, אַף לְאַחַר בַּת קוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second resolution to the contradiction in step 2, as an alternative to step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the statement to a specific תנא's opinion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: After the בת קול, no one could permit following בית שמאי.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי יהושע, a בת קול does not decide הלכה, so following בית שמאי is still permitted even after it.

steps.title: The difficulty with רבא's ruling stands
steps.stepSummary: Whatever we say about following בית שמאי or בית הלל, רבא's ruling is still a problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, it is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא comes back from the side discussion about בית שמאי and בית הלל and says the original problem has not gone away. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said that someone who takes the חומרות of both sides is a fool. רבא's ruling seemed to do just that, holding two stringencies that clash with each other. Whether or not one may follow בית שמאי, that does not explain רבא, so the question still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case; whatever we said before
It is difficult; the problem remains

phrases.english: In any case, it is difficult.
phrases.notes: He means רבא's ruling from the previous עמוד (דף מג עמוד ב), which seemed to take two clashing חומרות.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכׇּל מָקוֹם, קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the בית שמאי and בית הלל side discussion to the main problem with רבא's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling about the entrance of the וושט
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By the ברייתא, someone who takes two clashing חומרות is a fool, and רבא appears to have done exactly that.

steps.title: רבא followed רב completely
steps.stepSummary: רב טבות answers that רבא's whole ruling follows one consistent view, the view of רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב טבות said: He acted entirely according to רב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב טבות answers the difficulty. רבא did not mix two opinions; everything he ruled comes from רב alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The charge was that רבא took one חומרא from one view and a second חומרא from another view. רב טבות says both חומרות come from one person, רב. Holding both is therefore consistent, not foolish. The proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: All of it; the whole ruling
He did it; he ruled it

phrases.english: Rav Tavut said:
He did all of it according to Rav,
phrases.notes: "He" is רבא, whose ruling we just called difficult.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב טָבוּת: כּוּלַּהּ כְּרַב עַבְדַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty raised in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that both חומרות come from one consistent opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא mixed the חומרות of two opposing views.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both חומרות are רב's own view, so רבא followed one opinion fully.

steps.title: רמי בר יחזקאל reports what רב really said
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר יחזקאל says that רב held the entrance of the וושט is not a place of שחיטה, yet a hole there of any size makes the animal a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רמי בר יחזקאל came, he said: Do not listen to the rules that my brother רב יהודה stated in the name of רב. This is what רב really said: The חכמים gave a measure for the וושט. That shows the entrance of the וושט is not a place of שחיטה, and still רב says a hole there of any size makes it a טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings proof for רב טבות's answer. רמי בר יחזקאל corrects his brother's report and shows that רב himself held both חומרות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From רב יהודה's report, it sounded as if a hole there makes a טרפה only because the spot counts as a place of שחיטה. רמי says that is wrong: the spot is not a place of שחיטה, since the חכמים limited the valid area, and still a hole there of any size makes a טרפה. So both חומרות belong to רב, and רבא was simply following him.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not listen
General rules or principles
The entrance or top part of the וושט
A place where שחיטה is valid
With any amount, even a tiny hole
By inference; this shows that

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, the entrance of the וושט is not a place of שחיטה, yet any hole there makes the animal a טרפה. Both חומרות come from רב.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume that only a valid place of שחיטה can make the animal a טרפה when it is pierced. Here the two questions are separate: the spot is not valid for שחיטה, yet a hole there still makes a טרפה.

phrases.aramaic: דְּכִי אֲתָא רָמֵי בַּר יְחֶזְקֵאל אָמַר:
phrases.english: For when Rami bar Yechezkel came, he said:
Do not listen to these rules
that Yehuda my brother stated in the name of Rav!
phrases.notes: "Yehuda my brother" is רב יהודה, the brother of רמי בר יחזקאל.

phrases.english: This is what Rav said:
The gullet: the Sages gave [it] a measure,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording. The "measure" is the area of the וושט where שחיטה works.

phrases.english: which shows that the entrance of the gullet
is not a place of slaughter,
and yet he says: with any amount.
phrases.notes: He means that a hole there of any size makes the animal a טרפה.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּכִי אֲתָא רָמֵי בַּר יְחֶזְקֵאל אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source that proves רב טבות's claim.
steps.raayaObject: That רב himself held both חומרות about the entrance of the וושט
steps.raayaSupportSource: רמי בר יחזקאל's correct report of רב's words

steps.title: The upper limit for valid slaughter in the gullet
steps.stepSummary: How high up the וושט is שחיטה valid? רב נחמן says up to the point where only enough remains for a hand to grip.
steps.simpleTranslation: How far up? רב נחמן said: until there is only enough room left for a hand to grip.
steps.whatsHappening: Since we just heard that the חכמים gave the וושט a measure, the גמרא asks what that measure is. It starts with the top limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a side question that grows out of the last step. The upper limit is the spot below which the space left above is just enough for a hand to hold. Above that point is the תורבץ, which is not a place of שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: Upward; the top limit
Up to how far?
A hand's grip; enough room to hold it

phrases.english: Upward, until how far?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: עַד כְּדֵי תְּפִיסַת יָד.
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: Until there is enough for a hand to grip.
phrases.notes: He means until the top part of the וושט left above is just big enough for a hand to hold.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַעְלָה עַד כַּמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the "measure" mentioned in step 7 and asks for details.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The upper limit of the valid area for שחיטה in the וושט
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Until only enough room for a hand's grip remains above

steps.title: The lower limit for valid slaughter in the gullet
steps.stepSummary: How far down the וושט is שחיטה valid? רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, says until the place where it becomes hairy.
steps.simpleTranslation: How far down? רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: until it becomes hairy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks about the bottom limit of the valid area in the וושט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is that שחיטה works all the way down to where the וושט becomes hairy. That is where the כרס, the first stomach, begins. This answer is what the next step will challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Downward; the bottom limit
That it becomes hairy, where the כרס begins

phrases.english: Downward, until how far?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:
Until it becomes hairy.
phrases.notes: The inside lining of the כרס is hairy, so this means up to where the כרס opens.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַטָּה עַד כַּמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The matching question for the bottom limit, after step 8 asked about the top.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The lower limit of the valid area for שחיטה in the וושט
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Until the point where the וושט becomes hairy, at the opening of the כרס

steps.title: The bottom handbreadth counts as the stomach
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the lower limit: רב said the bottom טפח of the וושט is the inner כרס, so cutting there should be cutting in the כרס.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רבינא said in the name of גניבא, quoting רב: The טפח of the וושט next to the כרס is the inner כרס. So why is it allowed? When he cuts there, he is cutting in the כרס!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer about the lower limit. It quotes רב to show that the bottom part of the וושט is really part of the כרס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן allowed שחיטה all the way down to where the וושט becomes hairy. But according to רב, the last טפח before the כרס already has the status of the inner כרס. If so, cutting in that last טפח is cutting the כרס, not the וושט, and the שחיטה should not work.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? It opens a challenge
A handbreadth
The inner כרס; the inside part of the first stomach
Why?

phrases.english: Is that so?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רָבִינָא אָמַר גְּנִיבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: But didn't Ravina say in the name of Geneiva, quoting Rav:
A handbreadth in the gullet next to the rumen,
this is the inner rumen.
Why?
phrases.notes: He means: why did רב נחמן allow שחיטה all the way down to the hairy part?

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קָא שָׁחֵט בְּכָרֵס קָא שָׁחֵיט!
phrases.english: When he slaughters there, he is slaughtering in the rumen!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָאָמַר רָבִינָא אָמַר גְּנִיבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the lower limit given in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that שחיטה is valid down to where the וושט becomes hairy
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב said the bottom טפח of the וושט is the inner כרס, so cutting there is cutting the כרס, and the שחיטה should not count.

steps.title: Read רב's statement as talking about the top handbreadth of the rumen
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the wording of רב's statement. The inner כרס is the top טפח of the כרס next to the וושט, not the bottom טפח of the וושט itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say it this way: the handbreadth in the rumen that is next to the gullet is the inner rumen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 10 by changing the wording of רב's statement. The inner כרס starts inside the stomach, not inside the וושט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 10, רב seemed to say that the bottom טפח of the וושט is really the כרס, so שחיטה there should be invalid. With the new wording, that טפח belongs to the כרס, and the whole וושט down to where it gets hairy stays a valid place for שחיטה. Now רב and רבה בר אבוה no longer clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (read it this way). Used to fix the wording of a statement.
A handbreadth, a measure of length
The inner rumen, the upper part of the stomach. It is not a place for שחיטה.

phrases.english: Say: a handbreadth in the rumen
phrases.notes: The גמרא is changing רב's words. Before, it said 'a handbreadth in the וושט'; now read it as 'in the כרס'.

phrases.english: adjacent to the gullet,
this is the inner rumen.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא: טֶפַח בְּכָרֵס סָמוּךְ לַוֶּושֶׁט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 10 by changing the wording of רב's statement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב said the bottom טפח of the וושט itself is the inner כרס, so שחיטה there would be invalid.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב meant the top טפח of the כרס, next to the וושט. The whole וושט, down to where it becomes hairy, is valid for שחיטה.

steps.title: רב was talking about a bull, which is extra hairy
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: רב's statement is about a bull. In a bull, the hairy part reaches up into the bottom טפח of the וושט.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: when רב said this, he was talking about a bull, which is hairier.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different answer to the question from step 10. This time it keeps רב's original words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's words stay the same, but they apply only to a bull. In a bull, the hair already starts in the bottom טפח of the וושט. So רב and רבה בר אבוה agree on the real rule: the valid area ends where the hair begins. In other animals, the hair does not reach that high.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say this instead. It opens a second answer.
A bull or ox
Hairy

phrases.english: If you wish, say:
when Rav said it, it was about a bull,
which is more hairy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: כִּי קָאָמַר רַב – בְּתוֹרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 10, given instead of the answer in step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's rule about the bottom טפח seemed to apply to every animal and to clash with 'until it becomes hairy'.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב's rule applies to a bull, where the hair reaches into that טפח. Both sages agree the line is where the hair starts.
steps.whatToRemember: The bottom limit for שחיטה in the וושט is where it becomes hairy. רב's 'bottom טפח' statement either really means the top טפח of the כרס, or it is about a bull, whose hair starts higher.
steps.whyThisMatters: Both answers keep one clear rule for where שחיטה in the וושט stops being valid.

steps.title: If the top of the gullet is torn off the jaw, the animal is kosher
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן quotes שמואל: if the opening of the וושט is completely torn away from the jaw, the animal is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל: if the entrance of the gullet was completely detached from the jaw, the animal is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. שמואל rules that if the top opening of the וושט is torn loose from the jaw, the animal does not become a טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 dealt with a hole at the entrance of the וושט, which does make the animal a טרפה. Here the וושט is not pierced; it is only pulled loose from where it attaches to the jaw. שמואל says that kind of damage does not make the animal a טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: The entrance, or top opening, of the gullet
The jaw
Kosher, valid to eat

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said that Shmuel said:
The entrance of the gullet
that was completely detached from the jaw is kosher,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: תּוּרְבַּץ הַוֶּושֶׁט שֶׁנִּיטַּל כּוּלּוֹ מִלֶּחִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from where the וושט is valid for שחיטה to what happens when the top of the וושט is torn loose.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the entrance of the וושט is completely torn away from the jaw, the animal is כשר.

steps.title: A משנה supports שמואל: a detached lower jaw is kosher
steps.stepSummary: Support for שמואל is brought from a משנה that says an animal whose lower jaw was removed is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And our תנא also taught this: if the lower jaw was removed, the animal is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: A משנה is brought to back up שמואל's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the whole lower jaw is gone, the וושט must also have come loose from the jaw. Since the משנה still calls the animal כשר, it agrees with שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Our תנא (the משנה) also taught this. It brings support from a משנה.
The lower jaw

phrases.english: And our tanna also taught:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה that comes later in the מסכת, on דף נד.

phrases.english: If the lower jaw was removed, it is kosher.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּתְנָא תּוּנָא: נִיטַּל לֶחִי הַתַּחְתּוֹן – כָּשֵׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the ruling of step 13.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ruling that a וושט torn loose from the jaw is כשר
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: if the lower jaw was removed, the animal is כשר

steps.title: רב פפא objects: isn't this uprooting of the סימנים?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא challenges שמואל: a וושט torn off the jaw should count as uprooting of the סימנים, which makes an animal a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא challenged this: but isn't this a case of the סימנים being torn out of place?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא attacks שמואל's ruling. He argues that tearing the וושט loose from its place is uprooting of the סימנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the סימנים (the וושט and the windpipe) are torn out of their place, the animal is a טרפה. רב פפא says that pulling the top of the וושט off the jaw is exactly that, so the animal should not be כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged it, a strong objection to a ruling
The סימנים being torn out of their place
The two signs of שחיטה: the וושט and the windpipe

phrases.english: Rav Pappa objected to this:
But isn't there uprooting of the simanim?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב פָּפָּא: וְהָאִיכָּא עִיקּוּר סִימָנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's ruling from step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that a וושט torn off the jaw is כשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Tearing the וושט from its place is uprooting of the סימנים, which makes the animal invalid, so it should not be כשר.

steps.title: The משנה is a problem for רב פפא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns the question back on רב פפא: the משנה says a removed lower jaw is כשר, and that clashes with his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רב פפא, the משנה is difficult: it says if the lower jaw was removed, it is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps in and points out that רב פפא's objection runs into the משנה brought in step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the lower jaw is removed, the סימנים that are attached to it must come loose too. Even so, the משנה calls the animal כשר. So רב פפא's idea that this counts as uprooting of the סימנים seems to clash with the משנה itself.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult, it raises a problem
Our משנה

steps.confusionAlert: This question is aimed at רב פפא, not at שמואל. The משנה that supported שמואל in step 14 is now used against רב פפא's objection.

phrases.english: And according to Rav Pappa, the mishna is difficult:
If the lower jaw was removed, it is kosher.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַב פָּפָּא קַשְׁיָא מַתְנִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the challenge of step 15 back on רב פפא, using the משנה from step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that a וושט torn off the jaw counts as uprooting of the סימנים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A removed lower jaw also tears the סימנים loose, yet the משנה rules the animal כשר. So רב פפא's reasoning seems to contradict the משנה.

steps.title: The משנה fits רב פפא but challenges שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רב פפא can explain the משנה easily: his rule is about סימנים that were fully uprooted, and the משנה is about a jaw cut off above the סימנים. But the same case now looks hard for שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, the משנה is no problem for רב פפא. His rule is about סימנים that were truly uprooted, and the משנה is about a jaw cut off above the סימנים. But for שמואל it is a problem!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question it just asked against רב פפא. Then it turns the same difficulty back against שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא splits the cases on רב פפא's behalf: if the סימנים themselves are ripped out, the animal is טרפה, but the משנה is about a jaw cut off above them, so the סימנים are not touched. שמואל cannot use this split, because his case is a וושט torn completely off the jaw. That looks exactly like uprooting the סימנים, which makes an animal טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it makes sense for (one side, but not the other)
Were truly uprooted, ripped out completely
Was cut off / severed
The two organs cut in שחיטה: the וושט (food pipe) and the קנה (windpipe)

steps.confusionAlert: The step opens by defending רב פפא, but its main point is the last line: now the problem sits on שמואל.

phrases.english: Granted, the Mishnah for Rav Pappa
is not difficult:
this (his rule) is where they were completely uprooted;
phrases.notes: 'They' are the סימנים. When they are ripped right out, the animal is טרפה.

phrases.english: that (the Mishnah) is where it was severed
above the simanim.
But for Shmuel it is difficult!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא מַתְנִיתִין לְרַב פָּפָּא לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 16 for רב פפא, then turns the difficulty back onto שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling (Step 13) that a וושט torn completely off the jaw is כשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A וושט torn completely off the jaw is the same as uprooted סימנים, which make an animal טרפה. Unlike רב פפא, שמואל cannot say the tear was above the סימנים.

steps.title: שמואל meant mostly torn, not completely
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the wording of שמואל's ruling: the animal is כשר when the opening of the וושט was torn away for the most part, not entirely.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not say 'all of it'; say 'most of it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge against שמואל by changing one word in his statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the וושט were torn off completely, that would be uprooting, and the animal would be טרפה. By reading שמואל as 'most of it,' some connection is left, so the animal stays כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't say... rather say (the גמרא corrects the wording)
All of it
Most of it, the majority

phrases.english: Do not say 'all of it,'
rather say 'most of it.'

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תֵּימָא כּוּלּוֹ, אֶלָּא אֵימָא רוּבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against שמואל in Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל called the animal כשר even when the וושט was torn completely off the jaw.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל called it כשר only when most of it was torn away, so some connection remains.

steps.title: Another שמואל ruling: mostly detached סימנים are טרפה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a different statement of שמואל, reported by רבה בר בר חנה: סימנים detached in their majority make the animal טרפה. That seems to contradict the new 'most of it is כשר' reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of שמואל: סימנים that came loose for the most part make the animal טרפה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave, using another statement of שמואל himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 said שמואל holds that a mostly torn וושט is כשר. Here שמואל says outright that mostly detached סימנים are טרפה. So שמואל seems to contradict himself.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't [so-and-so] say? (opens a challenge)
Came loose, were detached
An animal with a fatal defect, which may not be eaten even after שחיטה

phrases.english: But didn't Rabba bar bar Ḥana say
that Shmuel said:
simanim that were detached in their majority
— a tereifah?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 18 using a contradicting statement of the same אמורא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading in Step 18 that שמואל calls a mostly torn וושט כשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל himself rules that סימנים detached in their majority make the animal טרפה, so he cannot also hold that 'most of it' torn is כשר.

steps.title: Peeled off versus pulled apart
steps.stepSummary: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי settles the contradiction. If the וושט was peeled off in one piece, the animal is כשר even when most of it is detached. If the סימנים were pulled apart and left hanging by scattered bits, the animal is טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי said: Here, where the animal is כשר, the וושט was peeled off. There, where it is טרפה, the סימנים were torn apart.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא answers the contradiction by showing that שמואל's two statements are about two different kinds of damage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the וושט is peeled off, the part that stays attached is all in one area, so it can heal and the animal is כשר. When the סימנים are pulled apart, they hang on by a few separate bits of flesh and cannot recover, so the animal is טרפה. Both statements of שמואל are true, each for its own case.

keyTerms.meaning: Was peeled off, folded back as one piece
Was pulled apart, torn loose in pieces
Here... there (splitting two cases)

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל: a וושט mostly peeled off in one piece is כשר. סימנים mostly pulled apart into scattered bits are טרפה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי
phrases.english: Rav Sheisha son of Rav Idi said:
This is where it was peeled off;
phrases.notes: 'This' is the 'most of it is כשר' ruling from Step 18.

phrases.english: there is where they were pulled apart.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי: הָא דְּאִקְּפַל אִיקְּפוֹלֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's two statements are about the same kind of damage, so they contradict.
steps.terutzMaskana: Peeling off in one piece (it can heal) is כשר; pulling apart into scattered pieces (it cannot heal) is טרפה.

steps.title: A cut windpipe: how much is needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next case in the משנה, a cut windpipe. It quotes a ברייתא: the windpipe must be cut through most of it for the animal to be טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'or a cut windpipe.' It was taught in a ברייתא: How much must the windpipe be cut? Most of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting the next words of the משנה, then brings a ברייתא that gives the size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה just says a cut windpipe is טרפה without saying how much. The ברייתא adds that it must be cut through the majority, so a small cut does not make the animal טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: A windpipe that was cut across
The windpipe (the קנה)
Through its majority, most of it

phrases.english: "Or a cut windpipe."
It was taught:
How much must the windpipe be cut?
Through its majority.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּפְסוּקַת הַגַּרְגֶּרֶת. תָּנָא: כַּמָּה פְּסוּקַת הַגַּרְגֶּרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the next phrase of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A windpipe cut through most of its width makes the animal טרפה.

steps.title: What counts as 'most' of the windpipe?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how 'most' of the windpipe is measured, and begins to bring רב's answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much is 'most of it'? רב said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a closer definition of 'majority.' It is setting up רב's answer, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing the rule is 'most of it' is not enough; the גמרא wants to know how to measure that majority on the windpipe. The answer is opened here with רב's name and continues in the following text.

keyTerms.meaning: And how much? (asks for an exact measure)
Its majority

phrases.english: And how much is its majority?
Rav said:

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכַמָּה רוּבָּה? רַב אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a closer definition of the 'majority' given in Step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the majority of the windpipe is measured for it to count as cut.
